pages.text:
Achintya Bhat 
Regn no: 201080077 
Branch: IT 
 
 
BNY Mellon visited our VJTI campus on 8th August 2022, to hire interns. I am very happy 
to say that I was selected for their internship program. I am sure you must be curious to 
know about their interview process and I am glad to share my experience. 
The selection process basically consisted of an online test and then 2 rounds of online 
interview. 
 
Eligibility: 
70 % or 7 CGPA and above in current graduating degree and 60% in 10th & 12th 
 
Online test 
The test was conducted on HackerRank. It consisted of 4 questions with different 
difficulty levels and the test duration was 90 mins. You could visit the question after 
submitting them and there was no separate time limit for each question. You could 
switch between questions which is quite a relief as you don’t need to plan how much 
time to allot to a question or whether to skip the present question or not.  Auto-
submission functionality was present and it is explained in detail here.   
Among those 4 questions, I was able to solve 3 questions(Q1, Q3, Q4). I remember only 
Q1, Q3 & Q4. 
Q1: There are n number of houses, each having a certain house number and distance 
from a point. You need to find 2 houses between which we can build the largest 
house.(I’m not quite sure whether this question was here or in some other test) 
Soln: Sort the houses based on their distances. Then find the distance between each pair 
of successive houses and find the one with the maximum distance between them. Then 
print their house numbers in ascending order. The solution passed all the test cases.

Q2) We have an array of integers. Find out the number of subarrays which when 
removed, the parent array has elements in ascending order. 
 
Soln: I tried brute-force here. I used 2 ‘for’ loops here where int i of the first loop was 
starting index and int j of the second loop was the last index. For each i, j, it checked 
whether the elements before ‘i’ were in order and those after ‘j’ were in order and if the 
element before ‘i' was less than that after ‘j’. If yes, it incremented the ‘count’ variable.  
I had also thought of an efficient solution in which if for certain value of i, j, if the 
elements are in order, then it is true for all subarrays with the same value of i and j 
greater than the current one. But I ran out of time so couldn’t implement it. 
 
Q3) Given an array of integer. The cost for this array is given as the number of times 
max is updated while iterating over the array. Given 3 values n(size of array), m(max. of 
the array), and the cost, find the number of arrays possible which have the given cost. 
 
Soln: This can be solved easily using dynamic programming.  I made 2 3D arrays, arr1 
and arr2. Here, arr1[i][j][k] indicates the number of arrays of size i whose max value is j 
and cost is k. And arr2[i][j][k] indicates the increase in number of arrays of size i and 
cost k when max is incremented by 1.  
We can write arr2[i][j][k] = j * arr2[i - 1][j][k] 
arr1[i][j][k] = arr2[i][1][k] + arr2[i][2][k] + … + arr2[i][j][k] = arr1[i][j-1][k] + 
arr2[i][j][k] 
The solution passed all the test cases. 
 
PPT: 
BNY Mellon did a presentation at our college on 8th August, 2022. It was the first 
company which was conducting an offline event and we were excited about it. However, 
we had to give a test for another company on the same day and so could not attend it. 
They sent the list of shortlisted candidates later that day and we had interviews on the 
same day. 
 
Interview round:

First Round: The interview was conducted online fortunately. We had to join from 
Teams and join Hackerrank codepair link. The camera was on the entire time. The 
interviewer was friendly and gave me time to answer each question. He did get annoyed 
a bit when for some questions, I didn’t give a direct answer. I don’t remember the 
questions correctly but have listed the ones I remember below: 
 Tell me about yourself. 
 Which languages are proficient in? How would you rate yourself for each of those 
languages? 
 What is scripting language and compiled language? Is Python a scripting 
language? 
 What is interface in java? Can an interface have a static field? (yes) 
 Name the 5 types of trees. 
 What is MariaDB? 
 Segmentation, semaphore, critical section. 
 What does viewport do in HTML?( this was wrt a project I was showing him) 
 Advantages of lists over arrays 
 Syntax to open a file in python 
Later, he asked me about my projects. He told me to open 2 of my projects and tell him 
about them. The 1st one was a dynamic website I made and which I hosted on github 
pages. He asked me questions about HTML, javascript and CSS. The 2nd project was a 
website for face detection. He asked me about the libraries I used, what this piece of 
code does, etc. He then told me to give a live demonstration of the project which I did. 
He told me to give different inputs to the program.  
After that, he gave me a coding problem which I had to solve on the HackerRank 
codepair link. I had to write a class with methods to compare integers, strings and 
arrays. I think he was checking my proficiency in C++ because others were not given 
this question and it was a simple question requiring just the knowledge of classes and 
functions. I completed it soon. 
Second round: My second round happened soon after the first one(in fact I was the first 
to give the 2nd round). Some of the questions which was asked in the 2nd round that I 
remember are: 
 Which languages are you good in?(I answered C/C++)  
 Can we pass variable number of parameters in functions like in printf? (Yes, we 
can using ellipsis ‘…’) 
 What are methods? 
 What do you know about BNY Mellon? 
 What domain are you interested in? 
Later, the interviewer gave me a coding question. The problem was like this:

You are given an array of integers. What is the maximum number of elements which you 
can remove from this array such that their sum is positive(> 0)? 
Eg, [3, -5, 1, -1, 2] 
Here, we can remove 4 elements [3, 1, -1, 2] as their sum = 5 > 0 
 Soln: First of all, I sorted the array. Then, I iterated over the sorted array, adding each 
element to the sum. When the sum becomes less than 0, we stop the loop and return the 
current index. 
And then, the interview ended. 
 
Results: 
Preliminary results were announced on the same day and the official offer came the 
following day. 6 students were selected including me and all of us soon confirmed our 
acceptance except one(who had already been placed in another company as intern and 
could not join as per TPO policy). 
 
That’s it. I’m glad I will be joining BNY as an intern next summer and to share my 
experience with you all. At the end, I would like to give some important tips: 
For coding round 
1. Practice DSA regularly. Some of the useful websites are Leetcode and 
GeeksForGeeks which you all must already be familiar with. Some of the 
important questions on Leetcode can be opened only with subscription which is 
costly. So, I have learnt mostly from GeeksForGeeks. What I like about 
GeeksForGeeks is that it has articles about almost all the algorithms used by 
competitive coders today which are not present in our textbooks. And this might 
be an unpopular opinion but I think solving dozens of problems everyday by 
yourself is a waste of time. Many a times, reading and understanding from a 
article is easier than writing the whole code for an algorithm and then spending a 
day or two to debug it because of a mistake in a for loop. Also, there is nothing 
wrong in seeing other people’s solution of a problem. Their solution might be 
more efficient, or more readable. Some of these algorithms were given by their 
discoverers as part of their PhD thesis. The whole human civilization was built 
from previous generation’s shoulders. 
2. Make your fundamentals strong. 
3. Try to become extremely proficient in any 1 language. For me, it was C/C++. 
Learn all the library functions available in that language. For C/C++, 
cppreference is a good website. Java, Python too have very good documentations.

4. For aptitude questions, Indiabix is a good website. 
5. Try to see that company’s previous interview questions if available. 
6. Get familiar with the platform. I failed to score much in my previous tests 
because I was not aware of some of the technical details. I wasn’t aware that on 
submitting, it showed the results instantly and that I could correct them. Also, 
solve questions from that platforms. Some companies put questions directly 
from the website. 
 
For interviews 
1. Stay calm and confident. If required, drink water before the interview. 
2. Be ready atleast 5 min before the meeting starts. There might be sudden changes 
or problems while joining and if it causes any further delay, it may affect their 
impression of you. 
3. Prepare answers to standard questions like ‘Tell me about yourself’. 
4. Try to give direct answers as much as possible. Don’t try bluffing around. 
5. Give real-world examples when explaining any concept. It shows that you have a 
good understanding of the concept. 
6. Do some basic research about the company. 
7. Finally, don’t worry if you do not perform well in some interviews inspite of 
preparing well. There are some factors which are beyond our control. Questions 
might be from topics which are our weak area, you couldn’t understand the 
question at the moment, etc. Try to do your best in every interview. Many 
companies come to VJTI each of them with a handsome package. 
 
All the best!
